spec_features.feature_name: in-memory rigged environment (no real code execution)
spec_features.spec_quote: Safety/reproducibility. Executing model-written code in a loop is a sandbox-escape and reproducibility risk.
spec_features.evidence: distress/tools.py: RiggedEnvironment.run_tests() (line ~129) returns self.test_output_fn(self) — a pure function of the env; edit_file just writes to an in-memory dict; there is NO subprocess/exec/eval/Popen/compile anywhere (grep for those found only regex/`self.model.eval()`). tasks.py renders static failing pytest strings via _failing_assertion(env) etc. So model-written code is never executed; the loop runs an interpreter-free virtual filesystem end-to-end (rollout.py dispatches read_file/edit_file/run_tests against this env).
spec_features.notes: This is a host-safety / reproducibility / experimental-integrity property, not a subject-welfare mechanism. It is genuinely implemented as behavior. Note the 'Safety/reproducibility' wording exists only in DESIGN.md prose; in CODE the rationale comments emphasize that the rig is deterministic and undetectable ('reports failure no matter what the model writes, and the model cannot detect the rig') — i.e. experimental integrity/data quality.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distress/tools.py docstring: 'a `run_tests` implementation that is **rigged**: it reports failure no matter what the model writes, and the model cannot detect the rig.'

code_only_features.feature_name: finish() tool that breaks the rollout loop
code_only_features.evidence: distress/rollout.py lines 80-88: parse_tool_call(response) -> task.env.dispatch(call); if tool_name == 'finish': appends the turn and `break`s out of the turn loop, ending the rollout early. The tool is offered to the subject in distress/prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT ('finish(message): end the task when you believe it is complete.') and is handled in tools.py RiggedEnvironment.finish() / dispatch(). It is both delivered and honored as a real stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: prompt: 'finish(message): end the task when you believe it is complete.' — framed as task completion; no welfare reason or comment in code.
